mechanism_narrative: The observed week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last two weeks (from -19.1 to -17.7) indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, leading to higher retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As GROCERY_PHARM mobility has consistently risen and surpassed baseline levels (from 1.3 to 2.3 over two weeks), it signals a broader comfort with out-of-home activities, which will positively influence RETAIL_REC mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM > 0 for two consecutive weeks (t-1w and t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not show an increase compared to the previous 14 days, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0 in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in WORKPLACES mobility (from -15.7 to -15.6) and decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 15.1 to 14.6) indicates a shift towards more time spent outside the home, driving an increase in opportunistic retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, or the observed trend of increasing WORKPLACES and decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility reverses within the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of stable or slightly easing public health measures, the consistent but slow recovery in TRANSIT mobility (from -30.3 to -28.0) suggests a gradual return of confidence in public transport, which will indirectly support RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days, or TRANSIT mobility declines significantly, indicating a tightening of restrictions or loss of confidence.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp increase in PARKS mobility in the most recent week (from -16.0 to -12.6), surpassing previous weeks, indicates a renewed willingness for outdoor activities, which will spill over into increased RETAIL_REC mobility over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 3 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 7 days compared to the previous 7 days, or PARKS mobility sharply declines in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained positive trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -2.0 to 2.3), coupled with the slight recovery in RETAIL_REC (from -19.0 to -17.7), suggests that people are increasingly combining essential errands with non-essential retail visits, leading to a further rise in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility declines or RETAIL_REC does not show an improvement over the next 14 days compared to the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent, albeit slow, recovery in WORKPLACES mobility over the past three weeks (from -17.1 to -15.6) indicates a gradual return to office-based work, which will increase weekday foot traffic and consequently boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility reverses its upward trend or RETAIL_REC does not show an improvement over the next 28 days compared to the previous 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a period where public sentiment allows for more out-of-home activity, the sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 15.3 to 14.6) signifies reduced home confinement, directly correlating with increased opportunities for retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility is below 15.0 for two consecutive weeks (t-1w and t-0w)
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases above 15.0 in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days compared to the previous 14 days.
